wire_delta.conclusion: Two wire blocks differ between draft 21 and draft 22. LOCATION_FILTER Parameter is a real wire change (#1913, #1953): the draft 21 length-prefixed form (Parameter Type, Length (vi64), optional StartGroup, StartObject, EndGroupDelta, EndObject, with the field count inferred from Length) is replaced by Parameter Type followed by an explicit Location Filter Type (vi64) in place of the Length field, which selects the fields that follow: 0x00 no filter, 0x01 relative StartGroup, 0x02 StartGroup and StartObject, 0x03 adds EndGroupDelta, 0x04 adds EndObject, 0x05 Next Object with no fields; any other Location Filter Type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, so encoders and decoders of 0x21 (top level and inside FILL_PARAMETERS) must change and sub-project B (the codec task) must cover it. PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Message is editorial: its field Track Namespace (..) is renamed Track Namespace Prefix (..) with the same Section 8.7 Track Namespace encoding and position, prefix matching was already the draft 21 behavior (Section 7.5 of draft 21), and the new statement that AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN is the only allowed parameter matches draft 21 Section 9.20.3, so the bytes on the wire are unchanged and no codec change is needed for it. No blocks were added or removed. The Next Object encoding also changed: draft 21 used StartGroup=0, StartObject=0 under the length-inferred form, while draft 22 uses Location Filter Type 0x05 and Type 0x02 with {0, 0} is now an absolute start.

for_wire_codecs_B: LOCATION_FILTER (Parameter Type 0x21): Location Filter Type (vi64) replaces the draft 21 Length field; 0x00 no filter, 0x01 relative StartGroup, 0x02 StartGroup and StartObject, 0x03 adds EndGroupDelta, 0x04 adds EndObject, 0x05 Next Object with no fields, and any other type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (draft 22 lines 5291-5311). The same encoding applies at top level and inside FILL_PARAMETERS.
Next Object is no longer encoded as StartGroup=0, StartObject=0: Type 0x02 with {0, 0} is an absolute start, so the draft 21 two-zero form must map to Type 0x05, not to 0x02.
PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Message: the field Track Namespace is renamed Track Namespace Prefix; the encoding and field position are unchanged.
extract_wire_blocks finds 41 wire blocks in each draft; 2 changed (LOCATION_FILTER Parameter, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Message) and the other 39 are identical, with none added or removed.

from_L1b: Modules: include/moq/interop/wire/moqlite06/{varint,framing,setup,announce,subscribe,group}.h; src/wire/moqlite06/*.cpp plus the internal src/wire/moqlite06/body_support.h; tests/golden/moqlite06_*_test.cpp and tests/golden/data/moqlite06_moqdev_vectors.txt. Only CMakeLists.txt changed among existing files (additions); audit CLI output for drafts 18, 21, 22 and the golden pins are unchanged.

Interfaces: read_varint/write_varint; read_string; DecodeLimits and kDefaultLimits; read_framed_body, write_framed_message, expect_body_consumed; EncodeError; stream type helpers; decode_/encode_ functions per message (SETUP, ANNOUNCE_REQUEST/OK/START/END/UPDATE, SUBSCRIBE/UPDATE/OK/END/DROP, GROUP, FRAME); build_setup returns optional; read_capabilities with probe_level/effective_role/effective_cost; zigzag_encode/zigzag_decode.

Decisions: the varint is the QUIC varint and non-minimal encodings are accepted on decode. DecodeLimits defaults: 1 MiB message, 64 KiB string, 64 parameters (moq.dev MAX_PARAMS), 1024 hops; the draft states no limits, so these are defensive caps. Strings are bytes with no UTF-8 check. FRAME is not wrapped in an outer Message Length. Type precedes Message Length for the six Type-prefixed messages. A body shortfall inside a complete Message Length is ProtocolViolation; only short input is NeedMore. Typed encoders refuse unrepresentable values and take trailing DecodeLimits. Raw encode_setup does not validate known-parameter value shapes so malformed SETUPs stay buildable; raw helpers write_framed_message and the field writers exist for malformed probes.

DEFERRED (a) to L1d: NeedMore offset/required is inconsistent: read_varint reports the full width from the start, read_string and read_framed_body report the body only, after the prefix. The streaming reader must treat NeedMore as wait for more and not rely on required, or normalise it.

DEFERRED (b) to L1d: an unknown ANNOUNCE Type is skipped by Message Length in moq.dev (announce.rs:801-825) but decode_announce_message returns InvalidValue without consuming (pinned by UnknownAnnounceTypeIsInvalidValueWhereMoqDevSkips); the session layer decides.
DEFERRED (c) to L1c: the draft text has form feeds at page breaks (the loader must handle them) and the audit regex needs exactly a 3-space figure indent.

Cross-check (d): thin. Only the SETUP bytes 05 01 04 02 40 64 and varints 63/64/16384 were usable Lite06 literals from moq.dev commit b8b0d235a99bddb9043f453c46c958362d6c9247 (MIT OR Apache-2.0); the ANNOUNCE_END vector is derived from the draft; the varint.rs:500-507 and subscriber.rs:3147 literals were not extracted. (e) No byte divergence was found between the draft figures and moq.dev, with two notation points resolved per moq.dev: (M1) Table 6 says "Path (s)" but the codec treats the Parameter Value as raw bytes with no nested length prefix, matching moq.dev setup.rs:236 set_bytes(PARAM_PATH, ...); (M2) moq.dev names the 0x0 subscribe response SUBSCRIBE_START (subscribe.rs:505), with bytes identical to the draft SUBSCRIBE_OK on Lite06 (one Group varint).
Out of scope (f), L2: TRACK, TRACK_INFO, FETCH, PROBE, GOAWAY and datagrams.
ACTION (g): docs/draft-lcurley-moq-lite-06.txt is untracked. The audit skips cleanly without it, but it must be committed (ask the user) before CI can run the audit un-skipped.

GAP (h): an ad hoc ASan+UBSan build of all moqlite06 sources and tests (125 tests) was clean in the final review, but CMake still has no sanitizer target for these tests (it exposes sanitizers only for the fuzz targets).
NOTE (M5) for L1d: encode_setup refuses a Path above max_string_length while decode_setup accepts it and only read_capabilities rejects it (typed/raw split).

FIXED after final review: decode_announce_message and decode_subscribe_response threw std::bad_variant_access on a Cursor whose absolute offset is near SIZE_MAX (read_varint can pass through OffsetOverflow); both now return the DecodeError, covered by Moqlite06Overflow.EveryDecoderReturnsAnErrorNearSizeMax.
